defects.description: Private worker nodes have no specified NAT or VPC endpoint connectivity for image pulls, AWS API calls, and telemetry export; the design needs an explicit private-cluster connectivity plan.
Specify the AWS Load Balancer Controller, Kubernetes Ingress/Service resources, target type, and health checks that implement the ALB-to-frontend connection.
Database security is incomplete: MySQL TLS, database/cache credentials, and security-group rules restricting access from workloads are not specified.
HPA and node scaling are requirements but lack an implementation choice; also identify how application instrumentation and trace-context propagation will feed the OpenTelemetry collector.

reviews.summary: A well-matched EKS migration preserves Helm and covers the requested data services and observability, but private-network connectivity and several deployment details need completion.

defects.description: The design does not identify worker-node or Fargate capacity, workload placement, or the controller and Kubernetes resources implementing ingress; an EKS cluster node alone does not establish a runnable, load-balanced deployment.

Distributed tracing is asserted but not implemented: the only observability edge carries logs and metrics, with no application instrumentation, collector, trace propagation, or trace export configuration.
No NAT or VPC endpoint strategy is defined for private workloads to pull images and reach required AWS services, including observability endpoints.

Workload AWS permissions and encrypted cache connections are unspecified; define least-privilege pod identity and Redis in-transit encryption rather than relying only on private placement and encryption at rest.

Resolve the availability assumption explicitly: multi-AZ workload placement, Redis replicas/failover, scaling, and actionable alarms are not described; the HTTPS certificate attachment is also unspecified.

reviews.summary: The managed service choices fit the migration, but compute, ingress, tracing, private connectivity, and workload security remain too underspecified for implementation.

defects.description: The publisher failure queue does not establish durable event replay as specified. A native Lambda DynamoDB-stream SQS failure destination contains batch metadata rather than the original records, and stream records expire after 24 hours; define full-payload preservation or reconciliation from durable order/outbox state.

Consumer DLQs cover processing failures but not SNS-to-SQS delivery failures. Configure subscription delivery DLQs and alarms so a failed subscription delivery cannot disappear after SNS exhausts its delivery policy.

Conditional insertion by a newly generated order ID does not establish idempotency across repeated POST requests. Specify a stable client idempotency key and durable mapping to the original order ID to prevent duplicate orders and downstream work.
Specify least-privilege Lambda roles, source-restricted SNS-to-SQS policies, and authorization that limits order lookup to the appropriate customer rather than merely requiring authentication.

reviews.summary: Independent queues provide strong failure isolation, but publisher recovery, subscription delivery failures, and request deduplication leave the no-silent-loss guarantee incomplete.

defects.description: The one-year failure-retention procedure is incomplete: SQS retains messages for at most 14 days, and no archival consumer is defined for the intake or failure-record DLQs. DynamoDB can retain workflow outcomes for a year, but that does not automatically preserve payloads stranded in those queues.
The intake DLQ has no explicit source-queue redrive connection or policy, and the failure-record DLQ lacks an explicit alarm; connect and monitor both recovery paths.
Make branch-local Retry/Catch placement explicit so an exhausted task failure is recorded within its branch rather than escaping and failing the entire Parallel state.

Document stable client request identifiers and the recovery sequence when persisting the order succeeds but StartExecution fails; an existing order record must not cause a retry to skip workflow startup.
Specify least-privilege execution roles and customer ownership checks for order lookup; Cognito authentication alone does not describe record-level authorization.

reviews.summary: Durable Standard workflows and persisted per-step outcomes provide a strong recovery foundation, but queue archival, redrive wiring, and retry-boundary details require clarification.

defects.description: Thumbnail output is written to the triggering bucket without a specified input-prefix filter or equivalent exclusion, creating a potential recursive invocation loop and unnecessary cost; separate original and thumbnail prefixes or buckets.

Durable replay of failed welcome-email events is not established. For a DynamoDB stream event source mapping, a native SQS failure destination contains batch metadata rather than the original subscriber records; define full-event preservation or a durable pending-email reconciliation mechanism.
The photo bucket has no reader delivery path; add a private CloudFront media origin or another explicit authorized read mechanism for photos and thumbnails.
Define cache behaviors for public post reads separately from authenticated or subscriber-specific routes, including authorization forwarding, cache keys, TTLs, and write invalidation.

A RESTful interface does not itself require the API Gateway REST API product, and WAF can also protect a CloudFront distribution in front of an HTTP API; direct WAF association with API Gateway REST APIs is the valid justification here.

reviews.summary: Edge caching, private static hosting, asynchronous welcome emails, and managed storage fit the blog well, but thumbnail filtering and stream-failure recovery need correction.

defects.description: The thumbnail function writes to the same bucket that emits ObjectCreated events, but no input-prefix filter or output exclusion is specified; generated thumbnails can trigger further invocations.

Subscriber persistence and synchronous SES sending form a dual write without a durable retry boundary. If subscriber creation succeeds and email sending fails, no outbox, stream consumer, or recovery process ensures that the welcome email is eventually sent.

The thumbnail failure DLQ is unconnected and no Lambda dead-letter or failure-destination configuration is specified; creating a queue alone does not preserve events after asynchronous retries are exhausted.

API requests bypass CloudFront and its global cache, leaving readers dependent on a us-east-1 API round trip. API Gateway stage caching is regional and provisioned, with charges even when idle; justify that tradeoff or cache public API reads at CloudFront to better meet global latency and low-cost goals.

Specify CloudFront OAC and bucket access policies, author-only write permissions, and the actual browser-to-S3 presigned upload connection; issuing a presigned URL is not itself a Lambda-to-S3 upload.
CloudWatch is listed without explicit failure alarms or operational connections, and there is no defined global delivery path for uploaded photos and thumbnails.

reviews.summary: The core serverless services are appropriate, but regional API caching, synchronous email delivery, recursive thumbnail risk, and an unconfigured failure queue weaken the latency, cost, and reliability goals.

preference.why: A preserves Kubernetes tooling while explicitly covering multi-AZ compute, pod identity, tracing, data-tier failover, and backups; B leaves several of those implementation foundations unresolved.

B's durable workflow and persisted per-step outcomes provide a stronger recovery ledger, whereas A leaves both publisher replay and SNS subscription delivery failures insufficiently protected; B still needs explicit queue archival and redrive details.

A better addresses global API-read latency through edge caching and decouples welcome emails from signup, while also specifying private static hosting and failure monitoring; both designs need thumbnail trigger filtering.
